tasks.short: Coordinate production and shipping recovery with colleagues, suppliers, and customers.

steps.what: Check affected orders, production progress, and shipment dates in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Read delay messages in {EMAIL} and identify causes and missing information.

loop.input: Delay messages and affected order identifiers.
loop.output: Cited causes, proposed dates, unresolved questions, and affected orders.
loop.check: Validate order identifiers and dates; show source passages; clerk checks consequential claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per message; unresolved conflicts return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Messages describe causes and conditional dates in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Discuss practical recovery options with department supervisors.
Discuss delivery alternatives and complaints with suppliers or customers.
Approve consequential commitments and record the recovery plan in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Send approved dates and responsibilities through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure an exception view in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; a bounded reader turns relevant {EMAIL} messages into a cited delay brief. People negotiate recovery, while the {WORKFLOW} records commitment approval and sends template confirmations containing only approved facts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order status and explanations arrive separately; resolving conflicting interests cannot be reduced to status rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing event feeds and approval features handle the structured work. Bounded text extraction makes message preparation feasible, with AI coding reducing connector development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier promises may be unreliable. Customer concessions, scarce capacity, and competing commitments still require negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which promise will preserve trust and which recovery option colleagues can actually deliver.

ambition.what: Early recovery options for customers whose orders are at risk.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling status to preparing recovery choices and negotiating exceptions. Final commitment rights stay with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Compare split shipment and later shipment options.
reach.learn: Transport constraints, incremental freight cost, and delivery reliability.

evidence.claim: Status views, approval routing, and approved template notifications are established deterministic patterns.
A documented loading-slot case shows coordination benefits; it does not establish production complaint automation.
Order text can be extracted into structured fields; this supports extraction feasibility, not reliable negotiation.

assumptions: Typical work uses operational records alongside messages and calls; the mail share is a prior, not a measured baseline.
External discussion stays within delegated authority; changed commitments require the approval shown.
Confirmations use approved recipients and templates; free-text model drafts are never sent automatically.
GDPR applies to personal contact data; EU AI Act obligations depend on the deployed functions.
Build ranges are indicative working-day effort for a limited pilot, not proven delivery times.
unknowns: Available order identifiers, event feeds, and message access.
Who may approve delivery changes, concessions, and extra freight.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
Actual time spent preparing, negotiating, and confirming recovery.
research_questions: What extraction accuracy is achievable for conditional dates and conflicting messages?
Which operational events reliably predict a missed shipment?
new_work: Check extracted causes and conditional dates.
Resolve unmatched orders and contradictory promises.
Maintain approval limits, templates, recipient rules, and connectors.

tasks.short: Maintain material availability and raise replenishment requests for production.

steps.what: Retrieve stock, reservations, and expected receipts from the {ERP}.
Run material requirements calculations against the production schedule in the {ERP}.
Investigate suspect stock balances with warehouse staff and physical checks.
Authorise inventory corrections in the {ERP}.
Select replenishment quantities and dates, considering shortages and approved supply options.
Enter the purchase requisition in {PROCUREMENT}.
Approve the purchase requisition for the purchasing team.

tasks.design: Configure material requirements and exception rules in the {ERP}, with a traceable inventory correction flow. A deterministic link creates requisitions in {PROCUREMENT}; existing approval rules govern release to purchasing, while people investigate physical discrepancies and unusual supply choices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inaccurate stock, lead times, and bills of materials make automatic proposals unreliable. Clerks bridge gaps between planning and purchasing records.
tasks.enabler_now: Material planning and requisition approvals already exist in standard systems. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and adding validation; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock errors, supplier unreliability, minimum quantities, and unapproved substitutes cannot be solved by cleaner calculations alone.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real shortage from bad records and recognise when a substitute needs technical approval.

ambition.what: Daily review of materials likely to stop production.

tasks.altitude: The week centres on material risks and inventory causes instead of requisition entry. Spending and substitution approval rights remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Propose safety-stock and lead-time changes for recurring shortages.
reach.learn: Demand variability, service targets, inventory cost, and supplier performance.
Receipt timing, stock movements, count controls, and unit conversions.

evidence.claim: Material requirements calculations, replenishment parameters, and requisition approvals are established system capabilities.
Integrated warehouse and transport records are commercially available; this does not prove manufacturing replenishment outcomes.

assumptions: The company has repeatable material demand and maintained bills of materials.
Routine receipt booking belongs to warehouse operations; this task handles availability and discrepancies.
Purchase order placement follows requisition approval and remains a purchasing task.
Personal data remains access-controlled under GDPR; employee monitoring changes require assessment under national rules.
Build ranges cover a pilot material group and exclude a full inventory data cleanup.
unknowns: Availability and licensing of existing material planning features.
Accuracy of stock, bills of materials, units, and replenishment parameters.
Whether {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} share records or need a connector.
Inventory adjustment, substitution, and purchasing approval limits.
research_questions: Which parameter errors most often produce false shortages?
Can existing system configuration remove requisition re-entry without custom code?
new_work: Maintain lead times, minimum quantities, units, and supplier mappings.
Review false shortages and repeated inventory adjustments.
Monitor connector failures and approval queues.

tasks.short: Review production progress with supervisors and agree necessary changes.

steps.what: Check completed work, work in progress, and missed milestones in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Prepare a progress brief in {DOCS} for the supervisor discussion.
Discuss actual progress, emerging problems, and practical constraints with supervisors.
Agree production changes, responsible people, and completion dates.
Enter agreed changes and actions in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: An exception view in the {OPS_SYSTEM} feeds a deterministic progress brief, replacing repeated document assembly. Supervisors and the clerk discuss constraints and approve structured changes; the {WORKFLOW} applies those changes and tracks action dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress data is often late, and the important explanation sits with supervisors. Preparing a common factual view takes time even when the discussion must remain human.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational reports and structured action forms can supply the meeting. Small generators and write-back connections are cheaper to build with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Supervisors must expose bad news and explain local constraints. A dashboard cannot establish whether reported progress is physically credible.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the question that reveals an unreported constraint and secure a realistic agreement across departments.

ambition.what: Same-shift review of newly blocked production work.

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to floor discussions and following through on difficult actions. The clerk can surface issues earlier; production approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess whether quality holds explain recurring production delays.
reach.learn: Hold reasons, release authority, traceability, and defect escalation.

evidence.claim: Progress dashboards, template briefs, structured approvals, and action tracking can be implemented without model reasoning.
The digest supplies no direct case demonstrating automation of production supervisor discussions.

assumptions: Production execution uses workflow 'other' because the supplied list has no production-execution workflow.
Preparation changes more than the conversation, consistent with the task's strong human-work prior.
Structured decisions are captured during approval; automatic meeting transcription is unnecessary.
External recovery uses the approved changes from this task rather than repeating the same decision.
GDPR and applicable national consultation rules govern any identifiable worker activity data.
Build ranges assume an existing production status feed and a limited department pilot.
unknowns: How quickly supervisors and operators record actual progress.
Which schedule changes supervisors may approve without escalation.
Whether action tracking already exists in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Employee consultation requirements for changed visibility of work activity.
research_questions: Which exception thresholds lead to useful discussions instead of alert fatigue?
Can the current system capture structured decisions during the existing meeting?
new_work: Correct stale progress and disputed exception flags.
Maintain milestone definitions and escalation thresholds.
Close actions and investigate repeated missed dates.
Check that dashboards support coordination rather than unsupported worker rankings.

tasks.short: Turn sales forecasts into feasible production commitments and timetables.

steps.what: Retrieve the approved sales forecast from the {ERP}.
Collect open orders, material availability, and routing times from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Collect supervisor confirmations of capacity limits and planned downtime through {EMAIL}.
Build a base production timetable in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Compare alternative sequences and commitment dates in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Review trade-offs and select a proposed timetable with supervisors.
Approve production commitments and the timetable in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Publish the approved timetable to departments through the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Connect forecast data from the {ERP} and constraints from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using the existing planning module for the base timetable. A deterministic solver on the {DATA_PLATFORM} compares bounded scenarios and validates capacity, materials, and frozen periods; the {WORKFLOW} captures approval before publication to the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forecasts, capacity calendars, and material constraints are inconsistently aligned. Spreadsheet scenarios are difficult to maintain when priorities or assumptions change.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning modules handle the base calculation, while deterministic solvers handle explicit constraints. AI coding lowers the cost of connecting data and building scenario comparisons without requiring model judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Forecast error, uncertain process times, and conflicting service priorities remain. Moving from machine capacity to person-level allocation requires a separate EU AI Act assessment and consideration of national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which commitments deserve protection when a mathematically feasible plan would create an unacceptable commercial or operational outcome.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding timetables to comparing explicit trade-offs and challenging assumptions. The clerk gains faster scenario preparation; final commitment and resource approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Compare the cost and service effects of alternative capacity plans.
reach.learn: Constraint modelling, sensitivity analysis, and the difference between forecast error and execution failure.

reach.task: Prepare demand-and-capacity choices for cross-functional planning.
reach.learn: Planning horizons, frozen periods, inventory exposure, and commitment policy.

evidence.claim: Production planning modules and deterministic constraint solvers can generate and compare schedules without language models.
Feasibility requires explicit constraints and validation; the digest provides no measured production scheduling implementation case.

assumptions: The existing planning module can generate a base timetable; missing capability would change the estimate.
The solver schedules orders, machines, and aggregate capacity, not workers by behaviour or personal traits.
Scenario runs have fixed horizons, time limits, and constraints; infeasibility returns a conflict report.
Validation checks material timing, precedence, capacity, frozen periods, and differences from the approved schedule.
Supervisors confirm capacity through structured forms, replacing repeated mailbox chasing.
GDPR applies wherever personal data is processed; national rules may require consultation for working-time or monitoring changes.
Build ranges cover one bounded production area and exclude extensive master-data repair.
unknowns: Existing planning module capabilities, licences, and interfaces.
Quality of routing times, changeover rules, capacity calendars, and material availability.
Planning horizon, frozen periods, objective priorities, and acceptable solve time.
Whether proposed changes affect individual working times or employee monitoring.
Required access approvals and employee consultation processes.
research_questions: Can existing planning configuration generate useful scenarios before a separate solver is justified?
Which constraints explain the largest gap between planned and actual completion?
How do scenario results change when forecast and process-time assumptions vary?
new_work: Maintain constraint definitions, priorities, and planning parameters.
Investigate infeasible scenarios and stale capacity confirmations.
Compare approved schedules with execution and adjust unreliable assumptions.
Monitor solver time limits, interface failures, and schedule version conflicts.

role.altitude: The role moves toward production exception coordination and preparation of defensible recovery choices. People retain negotiations, physical verification, and commitment approval; shared data feeds and approval records prevent duplicate preparation across tasks.
reach: Support logistics analysts with recovery comparisons.
Support supply chain managers with material-risk and capacity scenarios.
Work with quality control systems managers on delays caused by quality holds.
Support management analysts with evidence on recurring planning constraints.
skills_to_grow: Material planning parameters and inventory controls.
Data quality diagnosis and operational event definitions.
Approval configuration and integration exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a daily production-risk service that connects material shortages, blocked work, and threatened deliveries to feasible recovery choices for authorised decision-makers.
